title: Mixed-ring resolved Hom and tensor models
statement:
Let $S\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, and let $U$ denote restriction of scalars, on complexes and on the ordinary unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], total Hom [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex], K-flatness [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], K-injectivity [def-pur-kinjective-complex], derived tensor [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] and derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Let $C,T$ be arbitrary $B$-complexes, $q:Q\to T$ a K-flat resolution over $B$, and $I$ a K-injective $S$-complex. Give $J(Q,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(UQ,I)$ the $B$-action $(bh)(e)=h(be)$, and give $J(T,I)$ the same action. This action commutes with the Hom differential, and $J(Q,I)$ is K-injective over $B$. Precomposition with $q$ is a $B$-linear quasi-isomorphism $J(T,I)\to J(Q,I)$. More generally, for every quasi-isomorphism $t:T'\to T$ of $B$-complexes and every quasi-isomorphism $s:I'\to I$ of K-injective $S$-complexes, $h\mapsto s\circ h\circ Ut$ is a $B$-linear quasi-isomorphism $J(T,I')\to J(T',I)$. Thus these comparison maps give a well-defined bifunctor $( [T],[I])\mapsto[J(T,I)]$ from $D(B)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(S)$ to $D(B)$, independent of representatives through the canonical localization comparisons. Moreover, for every K-flat resolution $p:P\to C$ over $B$, both arrows in
$$\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_B T)\ \longleftarrow\ \operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_B Q)\ \longrightarrow\ \operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_B Q)$$
induced by $q$ and $p$ are quasi-isomorphisms. Their localized zigzag identifies $[\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_B Q)]$ with $[C]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}[T]$, canonically for all such resolutions. The complexes $\operatorname{Hom}_B^\bullet(C,J(Q,I))$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(U\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_B Q),I)$ therefore represent respectively $R\operatorname{Hom}_B([C],[J(T,I)])$ and $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(U([C]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}[T]),[I])$. No flatness of $B$ over $S$, boundedness, or perfectness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0A96 (lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective), mixed-ring adaptation of its proof; adjacent lemma-RHom-well-defined and the internal-Hom construction, with the ordinary-module K-flat tensor comparison.

proof.text: For any $B$-complex $L$ and $S$-complex $N$, the action $(bh)(e)=h(be)$ makes each product term of $J(L,N)$ a $B$-module: $b_1(b_2h)(e)=h(b_2b_1e)=((b_1b_2)h)(e)$, and the unit and additive laws follow by evaluation. Since $d_L(be)=b\,d_L(e)$, the Hom differential satisfies $d(bh)(e)=d_Nh(be)-(-1)^nh(b\,d_Le)=(b\,dh)(e)$. Thus it is a $B$-complex. Precomposition by a $B$-linear chain map and postcomposition by an $S$-linear chain map commute with this action and the differential. Restriction $U$ preserves and reflects quasi-isomorphisms: the cycles, boundaries and cohomology are the same underlying groups, and an $S$-linear bijection that is already $B$-linear has $B$-linear inverse. No flatness is involved.

source.place: Tag 0A8X, Hom differential; elementary mixed-ring scalar check

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-rhom-well-defined] on the one-point site with ring $S$, source map $Ut:UT'\to UT$, and the given map $s:I'\to I$ between K-injective $S$-complexes. By Step 1, $Ut$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The cited lemma says exactly that $h\mapsto s\circ h\circ Ut$ is an $S$-quasi-isomorphism. Step 1 makes it $B$-linear and reflects its quasi-isomorphism property back to $B$. In particular take $t=q$ and $s=1_I$ to obtain $J(T,I)\to J(Q,I)$. This comparison requires no K-flatness of $UT$ or $UQ$.

source.place: Tag 0A95, lemma-RHom-well-defined, ordinary modules on the one-point site

proof.text: Choose a functorial K-injective resolution $N\to R(N)$ over $S$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] on the small one-point site. The functor on pairs of complexes $(L,N)\mapsto[J(L,R(N))]$ is contravariant in $L$ and covariant in $N$, by composition of the formulas of Step 1. Step 2 makes it invert quasi-isomorphisms in both variables (the natural resolution maps show that $R$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] successively in the two variables, taking the other variable as functor-category parameter; natural isomorphisms there are pointwise isomorphisms. This yields $D(B)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D(S)\to D(B)$ with the stated identity and composition laws. If $I$ is already K-injective, $I\to R(I)$ compares $J(L,I)$ with this model by Step 2. For an arbitrary identification between K-injective representatives use [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]: it is represented uniquely up to homotopy, and an isomorphism gives a homotopy equivalence. Postcomposition carries a homotopy $h$ to the Hom homotopy $f\mapsto hf$; hence the comparison is independent of the representative. The uniqueness and natural-transformation clauses of the localization lemma make all these comparisons canonical.

source.place: Tag 0A95 and internal-Hom construction; injectives.tex Tag 079P; derived.tex Tag 070I

proof.text: Let $A$ be any acyclic $B$-complex. By [def-pc-module-kflat-complex], $\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_B Q)$ is acyclic; its restriction to $S$ is acyclic by Step 1. Use only the chain-isomorphism clause of [lem-trf-bimodule-chain-currying-descent], with $(A,T,N)=(A,Q,I)$, to identify the underlying $S$-complex of $\operatorname{Hom}_B^\bullet(A,J(Q,I))$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(U\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_B Q),I)$. Apply [lem-sc-module-hom-complex-quotient] on both sides in degree zero. This gives a bijection between $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(B)}(A,J(Q,I))$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(S)}(U\operatorname{Tot}(A\otimes_B Q),I)$. The latter is zero by [def-pur-kinjective-complex], since $I$ is K-injective over $S$. The former is therefore zero for every such $A$, which is precisely K-injectivity of $J(Q,I)$ over $B$. This is the acyclic-test argument of 0A96 with the rings kept distinct; the cited currying clause has no resolution or derived-model hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 0A96, lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective, mixed-ring version of the displayed proof

proof.text: Both $P$ and $Q$ are K-flat over $B$. Thus [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] makes $1_P\otimes q$ a quasi-isomorphism because $P$ is K-flat, and makes $p\otimes1_Q$ a quasi-isomorphism because $Q$ is K-flat. These are exactly the two arrows of the stated zigzag. Apply [lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor] with $R=A=B$, fixed second complex $T$ and first-factor resolution $P\to C$: $[\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_B T)]$ computes $[C]\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}[T]$. Invert the first arrow and compose with the second to identify this object with $[\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_B Q)]$. Clauses (2) and (3) of that lemma give independence of the first resolution and naturality for $q$; their composition law gives the same identification through any third resolution. This proves canonicity for all $P,Q$, not merely an abstract existence of an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 06Y6, lemma-derived-base-change, with the preceding K-flat construction and Tag 064L

proof.text: By Steps 2 and 4, $J(T,I)\to J(Q,I)$ is a K-injective resolution over $B$. The representative formula of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], specialized to the one-point $B$-site, therefore computes $R\operatorname{Hom}_B([C],[J(T,I)])$ by $\operatorname{Hom}_B^\bullet(C,J(Q,I))$. On the one-point $S$-site the same formula, now with the already K-injective target $I$, computes derived Hom from $U[\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_B Q)]$ by $\operatorname{Hom}_S^\bullet(U\operatorname{Tot}(C\otimes_B Q),I)$. Substitute the canonical tensor identification of Step 5 and use exact restriction from Step 1. These are the two claimed models. The representative-independence clause of that definition and Step 3 ensure compatibility with the stated localization comparisons.

Source check: sites-cohomology.tex lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective = 0A96 and lemma-RHom-well-defined = 0A95 (tags lines 12939/12938). The 0A96 proof is the acyclic test, and Step 4 reproduces it with S and B kept separate. Steps 1-6 check out. (1) The B-action (bh)(e)=h(be) is S-linear because B is commutative and S acts through S→B; the differential sign is consistent with def-sc-module-total-hom-complex; U preserves and reflects quasi-isomorphisms. (2) lem-pur-rhom-well-defined on the one-point S-site, with s a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives and t=Ut, gives the comparison maps; directions match and no K-flatness of UT is needed. (3) A functorial resolution (prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist) and the localization universal property (1)-(3) applied one variable at a time give the bifunctor; lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived turns quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives into homotopy equivalences. (4) Tot(A⊗_B Q) is acyclic because Q is B-K-flat. The unconditional chain-isomorphism clause of lem-trf-bimodule-chain-currying-descent, plus lem-sc-module-hom-complex-quotient on H^0, carries the S-side vanishing to Hom_K(B)(A,J(Q,I))=0. (5) The zigzag arrows are quasi-isomorphisms by B-K-flatness of P and of Q respectively; lem-pc-derived-tensor-second-factor-functor with R=A=B, clauses (2)-(3), makes the identification canonical. (6) def-pur-derived-internal-hom on both one-point sites gives the two Hom models. Small cases: for S=B, Q=B[0] the item is 0A96. For Z→F_p, T=Q=F_p[0], I=(Q→Q/Z), J has Z/p in degree 1, which is Ext^1, and is K-injective over F_p. Zero inputs give zero. Duplicate search: def-trf-derived-coinduction is the special case T=B[0]; the pur/coef Hom-K-flat-into-K-injective nodes are one-ring; nothing else states this.
